Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:11:1.hebrew: אינן בכלל ברכה - ואע"פ שעם שבשדות בכלל ברכה, הני דמצו למיתי קמי כהנים, ויפנו כהנים אליהם ויברכום, והם לא באו — אינן בכלל ברכה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:11:1.english: They are not included in the blessing - Even though people who are in the fields are included in the blessing, these, who are able to come before the priests, so that the priests would turn to them and bless them, but they did not come — are not included in the blessing.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:12:1.hebrew: אבל דעיר לא - משום דלא אניסי, ויכולין להסדיר תפלתן:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:12:1.english: But [those] of the city — no - Because they are not constrained [by work], and they are able to arrange their prayer.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:1:1.hebrew: כי סליק רבי אבא מימי - שהפליג בספינה לים, וחזר:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:1:1.english: When Rabbi Abba came up from the seas - For he had sailed in a ship out to sea, and returned.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:1:2.hebrew: בברכות של ר"ה - לקמן מפרש מ"ש הני:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:1:2.english: Regarding the blessings of Rosh Hashanah - Below, [the Gemara] explains what distinguishes these [blessings from the others].

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:3:1.hebrew: מאן מודים - לו, לרבן גמליאל, בברכות של ר"ה ויוה"כ — ר"מ:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:3:1.english: Who concedes - to him, to Rabban Gamliel, regarding the blessings of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur — Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:3:2.hebrew: והלכה מכלל דפליגי - דקאמר ר' יוחנן הלכה כרבן [גמליאל] — בהך דמשמע מכלל דעמדו במחלוקתן:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:3:2.english: “And the halakha” — by inference that they disagree - For Rabbi Yoḥanan said, “The halakha is in accordance with Rabban [Gamliel]” — in this [statement], which implies by inference that [the Sages] still stand in their disagreement.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:3:3.english: The Rabbis - The other Sages, aside from Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:1.hebrew: אילימא משום דנפישי קראי - דאיכא דמוספי ר"ה ור"ח ומלכיות וזכרונות ושופרות:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:1.english: If we say it is because of the many verses - For there are the Musaf [prayers] of Rosh Hashanah and Rosh Chodesh, and [the verses of] Malchiyot, Zichronot, and Shofarot.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:2.hebrew: כיון שאמר ובתורתך כתוב - כלומר, כיון שאמר "נעשה ונקריב לפניך כמצות רצונך, כמו שכתבת עלינו בתורתך":
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:2.english: Once one has said, “And in Your Torah it is written” - That is, once one has said, “We will perform and offer before You in accordance with the commandment of Your will, as You have written about us in Your Torah.”

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:3.hebrew: אין צריך - לומר מקראות של המוספין:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:3.english: It is not necessary - to recite the verses of the Musaf [prayers].

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:4.hebrew: אלא משום דאוושי - שהרי כאן תשע, וארוכות, ומטעות, דאין הכל בקיאין בהן. ורבותי מפרשין להא דרב חננאל במלכיות וזכרונות ושופרות, וקשיא לי: הא דלא כרבנן, ולא כר' יוחנן בן נורי, דתנן (לעיל ראש השנה דף לב.) אין פוחתין מעשרה מלכיות וכו':
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:4.english: Rather, because they are numerous - For here there are nine [blessings], and they are long, and they cause error, since not everyone is well versed in them. And my teachers explain this statement of Rav Chananel as referring to Malchuyot, Zichronot, and Shofarot; but this is difficult for me, as it is neither like the Rabbis nor like Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, for we learned (above, Rosh Hashanah 32a): "One may not recite fewer than ten verses of Malchuyot," etc.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:8:1.hebrew: מתלתין לתלתין - שהיה מחזר תלמודו כל שלשים יום:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:8:1.english: From thirty [days] to thirty [days] - For he would review his learning every thirty days.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:9:1.hebrew: פוטר היה כו' - שש"צ מוציאם:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 35a:9:1.english: He would exempt, etc. - The prayer leader fulfills the obligation on their behalf.

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:1.hebrew: אילימא משום דנפישי - פירש בקונטרס: דאיכא דמוספי ר"ח וראש השנה, ומלכיות וזכרונות ושופרות. כיון שאמר "ובתורתך כתוב לאמר", כיון שאמר "נעשה ונקריב לפניך כמצות רצונך, כמו שכתבת עלינו בתורתך" — אין צריך לומר מקראות המוספין. ובשם רבותיו פירש להא דרב חננאל במלכיות זכרונות ושופרות. וקשה: הא דלא כרבנן, ודלא כר' יוחנן בן נורי, דתנן (לעיל ראש השנה לב.): אין פוחתין מעשרה מלכיות כו'. ור"ת פירש דאפסוקי דמלכיות זכרונות ושופרות קאי, והיכא דהתחיל פליגי, דלא יפחות למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה; אבל יכול לפטור עצמו לגמרי ע"י בתורתך כתוב לאמר. אבל מקראות של מוסף צריך להזכיר לעולם, שהם במקום הקרבנות. אבל מוסף דר"ח אין צריך להזכיר בר"ה, אלא שדי לו במה שאמר "מלבד עולת החדש ומנחתה", שבזה נכלל כל מוספי ר"ח העולות; וכדי להזכיר גם השעיר שהוא חטאת יאמר "ושני שעירים לכפר ושני תמידים כהלכתן":
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 35a:5:1.english: If we say, because they are many - Rashi explained: Because there are the Musaf offerings of Rosh Chodesh and of Rosh Hashanah, and [the verses of] Malkhiyot, Zikhronot, and Shofarot. Once one has said, "And in Your Torah it is written, saying," — once one has said, "We will make and offer before You, in accordance with the command of Your will, as You wrote for us in Your Torah" — one need not recite the Musaf verses. And in the name of his teachers, [Rashi] explained Rav Chananel's statement as referring to Malkhiyot, Zikhronot, and Shofarot. But this is difficult: [that statement] is not in accordance with the Rabbis, nor with Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, as we learned (above, Rosh Hashanah 32a): "One does not recite fewer than ten verses of Malkhiyot," etc. Rabbeinu Tam explained that [Rav Chananel's statement] refers to the verses of Malkhiyot, Zikhronot, and Shofarot, and where one has begun [reciting them], [the Tannaim] disagree, [in that] one may not reduce [the number of verses] — according to one Sage as he holds, and according to the other as he holds; but one can exempt oneself entirely by [saying] "And in Your Torah it is written, saying." But the Musaf verses must always be mentioned, because they stand in place of the offerings. However, the Musaf of Rosh Chodesh need not be mentioned on Rosh Hashanah; it suffices for him to say, "besides the burnt offering of the month and its meal offering," in which all the Rosh Chodesh Musaf offerings, the burnt offerings, are included. And in order to mention also the goat, which is a sin offering, he should say, "and two goats to atone, and two daily offerings according to their law."
